core_meaning.primary_meaning: Aasmaa represents Arabic أسماء (Asmāʾ), the plural of اسم (“name”); “sky/heavens” is not the literal meaning of this Arabic form.
core_meaning.literal_meaning: Arabic plural form of اسم (“name”); its use as a personal name is a separate naming convention.
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: Arabic أسماء (Asmāʾ) is the plural of اسم (“name”). The earlier gloss “heaven/sky/celestial realm” was inconsistent with this lexical form and has been removed. Asmāʾ is also an established feminine personal name, including the historical bearer Asmāʾ bint Abī Bakr. No derivation from the root س م و or a literal meaning “sky” is asserted here.

pashto.name: اسما

arabic.name: أسماء

faq.a: Aasmaa represents Arabic أسماء (Asmāʾ), the plural of اسم (“name”). It should not be glossed literally as “sky.”

faq.q: What is the origin of Aasmaa?
faq.a: The recorded form أسماء is Arabic. It is also an established feminine personal name in Muslim naming traditions.
Yes. The underlying Arabic form recorded here is أسماء (Asmāʾ).

faq.q: What is the root of Aasmaa?
faq.a: This record identifies أسماء as the plural of اسم; it does not assert a deeper root derivation.
Asmāʾ is used as a feminine personal name, but the literal lexical form is the plural of “name,” not an exclusively religious title.
This record does not establish the Latin spelling Aasmaa as a Qur'anic personal name; Arabic origin and Muslim usage are not sufficient proof of scriptural status.

faq.q: What does Aasmaa mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu script it is written اسماء. The literal Arabic lexical sense is the plural of اسم (“name”), not “آسمان/فلک.”
The supplied romanization is approximate; the Arabic form is commonly transliterated Asmāʾ, with spelling variants in Latin script.

faq.q: Is Aasmaa a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: The record classifies Aasmaa as feminine, consistent with established use of Asmāʾ as a feminine personal name; regional frequency data is not provided.
